subject: Ephemeral accelerator bridge + negotiated overage credit request
messages:
From: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay@peregrinelabs.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@peregrinelabs.com, eve.duncan@legal.peregrinelabs.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term access to HBM-optimized accelerator + billing flexibility

Karthik / Lauren —

Thanks for the productive call earlier. Quick note to put the ask in writing so procurement can move faster on our side. Our engineering spike next week needs transient access to a small pool of HBM-optimized H100-like instances (we expect ~600 GPU-hours over a 10-day window). Two asks:

1) Allow a temporary accelerator substitution (ephemeral bridge) from our reserved A100 family to an HBM-optimized H100 tier for that 10-day window and guarantee no preemption for the spike.
2) Provide a negotiated overage credit or invoice offset for any transient overage we incur on top of the reserved commit for the first month — we are asking for a one-time 20% overage credit (or $35k cap), whichever is smaller, to help us validate the model performance before converting to a longer reservation.

We realize both are non-standard. If you need an exec sign-off or a short SLA exception, please advise next steps. Procurement and Legal are on this thread (Eve).

Thanks,
Sanjay
Senior ML Engineer
Peregrine Labs
(Attachment: peregrine_capacity_request_v1.pdf)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay@peregrinelabs.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, eve.duncan@legal.peregrinelabs.com, procurement@peregrinelabs.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term access to HBM-optimized accelerator + billing flexibility

Sanjay —

Appreciate the write-up and the head's up. Putting this into the deal desk queue for an exception. Two clarifying points so we can route appropriately:

- When you say "no preemption" for the 10-day window, do you mean a hard non-preemptible SLA (we'd need to provision dedicated backfill or reservation hold) or just a prioritized scheduling with fallback to a lower-tier accelerator?
- Confirm estimated peak concurrent GPUs and whether the 600 GPU-hours is concentrated (e.g., 60 GPUs for 10 hours) or spread across the window.

Looping in Lauren and Marissa for the deal and exec path. I expect this will need a short exec approval (reservation hold + temporary hardware swap) and a negotiated overage offset. Vivek, can you review whether we can do (a) a 30-day reservation hold on current capacity, (b) permit ephemeral H100-like variants for the 10-day window, and (c) set a one-time overage credit (we'll propose a structure to legal)?

I'll share Peregrine's capacity plan once I have the concurrency details.

—Karthik
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay@peregrinelabs.com>, eve.duncan@legal.peregrinelabs.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term access to HBM-optimized accelerator + billing flexibility

Karthik / team —

Thanks for flagging. I'm supportive of a limited concession here to preserve the deal momentum — quick proposal for deal desk / exec: 

- Reservation hold: 30-day soft hold on their existing dedicated pool (prevents reassignments for that period).
- Ephemeral accelerator bridge: allow up to 80 GPU-hours concurrently on HBM-optimized variants for a 10-day window; if additional capacity needed, fallback to T4-like burst.
- Overaged spend concession: one-time invoice credit equal to 20% of overage charges for the first billing period post-window, with an absolute cap of $35,000.
- Conditions: customer signs an SLA exception addendum and commits to a short follow-up commercial review within 30 days post-spike.

If Legal is comfortable with the addendum and Finance signs off on the credit cap, I can escalate to Vivek for final exec approval.

Notes: keeping the cap protects us while the percentage helps Peregrine validate model economics.

-Lauren
VP, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay@peregrinelabs.com>, eve.duncan@legal.peregrinelabs.com, procurement@peregrinelabs.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term access to HBM-optimized accelerator + billing flexibility

Lauren / team —

I reviewed the numbers with Finance. Operationally we can do the 30-day soft hold and ephemeral bridge with these caveats: 

- The hold requires a refundable guardrail: if Peregrine cancels the reservation hold less than 7 days before window start, they pay a 50% hold fee on the estimated lost-utilization.
- The $35k cap is OK but must be applied as an invoice credit against the overage line item in the billing system (Finance requires a GL memo).
- We need an SLA exception addendum; Legal (Eve) should redline and push through DocuSign. I attached a starting redline (redline-sla-exception.docx) with the following changes:
  * Limited non-preemption clause tied only to the 10-day window and specific GPU IDs.
  * Explicit reconciliation clause for overage calculation (30-day billing lookback to confirm baseline).

If Peregrine accepts those bullets, we can route to exec for sign-off today.

-Marissa
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redline-sla-exception.docx)

2) Ephemeral accelerator bridge: allow up to 80 concurrent HBM-optimized GPUs for the 10-day window. If utilization spikes above that, automatic fallback to mixed TensorCore instances will execute; customer will be notified 1 hour before fallback.

Conditions: customer must sign the SLA exception addendum (legal redlines accepted) and acknowledge the fallback behavior in writing. Karthik, please confirm acceptance and ask them to sign via the DocuSign link.

Approving now to keep momentum. Vivek
